title: Real Grothendieck constant
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
formal: Determine the real Grothendieck constant \(K_{G}^{\mathbb R}\), defined as the least universal comparison factor between the vector and sign bilinear optima below.
definitions: For positive integers m,n and a real matrix \(A=(a_{ij})\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), define \(S(A)=\max_{\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}^{m},\,\delta\in\{-1,1\}^{n}}|\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sum_{j=1}^{n}a_{ij}\varepsilon_i\delta_j|\) and \(V(A)=\max_{u_1,\ldots,u_m,v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^{m+n},\,\|u_i\|_2=\|v_j\|_2=1}|\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sum_{j=1}^{n}a_{ij}\langle u_i,v_j\rangle|\). The inner product and norm are Euclidean. Define \(K_{G}^{\mathbb R}=\sup_{m,n\ge1,\,A\ne0}V(A)/S(A)\). The denominator is positive for nonzero A. Grothendieck’s inequality makes the supremum finite. The vector dimension m+n permits every possible Gram matrix of these m+n vectors; this is the unrestricted real constant, with no fixed dimension, complex vectors, computational restriction, or asymptotic input model.

context_blocks.text: The two optima compare a discrete sign assignment with its vector relaxation. The universal loss quantifies a basic limitation of this relaxation across all real bilinear objectives.

The earlier strict improvement over Krivine’s bound disproved a proposed value without determining the constant. A 2026 preprint reports a lower bound of \(6\pi/11\) and a further quantitative upper bound; their separation still exceeds the benchmark tolerance.

why: Determining this constant would settle a foundational quantitative barrier shared by functional analysis, semidefinite optimization and quantum correlations.

progress.text: Braverman, Makarychev, Makarychev and Naor prove a strict improvement over Krivine’s upper bound.
A preprint reports \(6\pi/11\le K_G^{\mathbb R}\le\pi/(2\log(1+\sqrt2))-10^{-4}\); these claims do not determine the constant to absolute error 0.01.

answer_criterion: Supply a real number a and a complete Lean-checked proof that its absolute difference from the defined constant is at most \(1/100\). A proved containing interval of width at most \(1/50\) qualifies through its midpoint. The constant is unconditional: a lower bound relying on an unproved complexity assumption settles only the corresponding conditional statement. Merely restating the defining infimum is not a determination.

sentences: The real Grothendieck constant compares the best vector assignment with the best sign assignment for a bilinear objective.
The supremum ranges over every finite real matrix, so fixed-dimensional constants are different targets.
The 2011 breakthrough disproved the proposed optimality of Krivine’s bound.
A 2026 preprint reports further improvements while leaving a substantial interval.
The benchmark requires a certified numerical estimate within absolute error 0.01.
